answer.location_description: A thin horizontal band spanning the full width near the top edge of the image, mainly rows 1-2, possibly extending to row 3.
answer.shortcut_type: horizontal bright line/band artifact at top edge
answer.mechanism: Several first-layer units have row-wide, same-sign weights confined to the top rows, unlike the rest of their weight maps. Units 25, 14 and 5 have strongly positive weights along row 1. Through layer 2 each has a net negative (benign) effect on the logit: roughly -20k, -10k and -15k in integer-product units. The malignancy-detecting central-blob units have negative weights on row 2, so a bright top band also suppresses them; this is clear for unit 3 and weaker for unit 27, whose net effect is about zero. Unit 30 also has positive row-1 weights and pushes toward malignant. Summing these approximate pathway effects, bright pixels in rows 1-2 push the logit toward benign. This ignores ReLU gating, so it is a rough estimate.
answer.evidence: Row-1 weight sums are far above what random weights would give (about 3 SD). Unit 25 sums to +823, with almost every value in cols 0-20 positive and values up to 95. Unit 14 sums to +755, unit 30 to +721, and unit 5 to +662. Row 2 is strongly negative in unit 27 (sum -835, with 21 of 24 weights negative) and in unit 3 (sum -406). Unit 27's row 1 is also negative (sum -458). The other edges of these same units (bottom rows, left and right columns) show no comparable coherent band. The center units have positive weights over the nodule area but negative weights specifically along the top rows. Effective output weights of the top-band units: unit 25 ≈ -20k, unit 5 ≈ -15k, unit 14 ≈ -10k, unit 30 ≈ +23k. Weighted by their row-1 sums, the net effect is benign.
answer.main_feature: The genuine signal is the brightness and extent of the central nodule. Units 3, 8, 21, 24, 27 and 28 have broad positive weights over the image centre, and unit 3's net path is toward malignant (about +15k). Units 2, 5 and 29 respond to a centre-dark, bright-surround pattern, which pushes toward benign. Larger, denser central nodules therefore read as malignant.
